messages:
omar (Platform): Heads-up — I'm putting together a proposal for a unified reliability taxonomy + dashboard to capture timeouts / 5xx / OOM / degraded-mode / fallback counts across runtime and infra. Need cross-team inputs.

maria (Eng-ML): Nice. Do you mean one dashboard that spans hosted/dedicated/private?

omar (Platform): Yes. Single source for high-level health, with drilldowns. Want consistent metric names + tag schema so product/console can filter by rollout, model, route, region, deployment_type.

kevin (Eng-Runtime): A few practical constraints: runtime can emit fine-grained events (per-request), but cardinality is our enemy. We should pick low-cardinality tags for dashboards.

ryan (Eng-SRE): +1. Also want clear alerting signals. Not just raw counts — need rate and relative deltas vs baseline.

eldar (Observability): Draft metric names I propose:
```
runtime.request_timeout.count
http.5xx.count
runtime.oom.count
fallback.invoked.count
degraded.mode.count
request.duration.ms (histogram)
```
Tags: service, route, model_family, region, deployment_type, rollout_id, error_class (timeout|5xx|oom|fallback)

sophie (Product): From console UX: we want to show a rollout overlay when a rollout_id is selected and annotate when fallback rate spikes. Also ability to pin alerts to a route.

maria (Eng-ML): model_family is OK, but model_hash or full model name will blow up metrics. Use family + version bucket.

kevin (Eng-Runtime): For OOMs we should include gpu_pool or queue_name tag (low cardinality). OOMs sometimes need memory metrics as well, but not on every metric emission.

omar (Platform): Good call. Proposal: two-tier telemetry approach:
- low-cardinality counters & histograms with agreed tags for dashboards/alerts
- high-cardinality events (detailed traces/logs) shipped to logs/traces with trace_id to correlate
This avoids metric explosion but keeps ability to investigate.

ryan (Eng-SRE): Agree. For alerts, prefer signals computed from the low-cardinality metrics. Examples:
- http.5xx.rate (1m) > baseline*3 for 5m
- runtime.request_timeout.rate > 0.5% for 10m (service-level)
- fallback.invoked.rate > 0.5% or absolute > 50/min
- sudden OOM spike (oom.count increases by >X in 2m)

eldar (Observability): Also recommend storing sample traces for every 1k errors (configurable), with higher sampling for customer-impacting routes.

kevin (Eng-Runtime): Implementation notes: runtime will emit counters like:
```
emit_counter("runtime.request_timeout.count", 1, tags={"route":"/v1/generate","model_family":"llama2","deployment_type":"hosted","region":"us-west-2","rollout_id":"r-2026-03-01"})
```
We can derive error_class in runtime before emitting.

maria (Eng-ML): We'll need to ensure model-serving wrappers add model_family + version_bucket automatically. I'll PR the wrapper change.

omar (Platform): Who owns the dashboard? My suggestion: eng-platform (ownership), eng-sre for alerts, eng-runtime + observability to own instrumentation. Product to sign off on UX.

sophie (Product): Fine with that. Product will provide two dashboard lenses: "Customer impact" (fallbacks, 5xx, timeouts) and "Infrastructure" (OOMs, queue lengths, degraded-mode durations).

ryan (Eng-SRE): For SLO conversations, can we add derived metrics: error_ratio by route/model_family and burn_rate? We'll need to compute error_ratio = 5xx.count / request.count.

eldar (Observability): We'll add computed metrics in the metrics pipeline to avoid duplicating logic client-side. Add request.count and request.success.count as base metrics.

kevin (Eng-Runtime): One more runtime constraint: degraded-mode is sometimes an internal behavior (e.g., fallback to smaller model). We need a clear boolean metric: degraded.mode.invoked (counter) + degraded.mode.duration_ms (histogram).

omar (Platform): Good. Also need to capture fallback reason tags: e.g., "fallback_reason":"oom|latency|policy" but keep it low-card (limited set).

maria (Eng-ML): For A/B rollouts we want to be able to slice by rollout_id and compare error rates side-by-side. That implies rollout_id must be present on low-cardinality metrics. Is rollout count large? We probably are safe because concurrent rollouts are limited.

kevin (Eng-Runtime): Rollout_id is OK as long as we expire old ones after 30d and avoid customer_id as a tag. For customer-level debugging, use logs/traces.

omar (Platform): UX asks: console should surface top 10 routes by fallback rate, allow filtering by model_family, and show timeline with rollout annotations. Product to provide mock.

sophie (Product): I'll drop a short mock in #product-assets by EOD.

ryan (Eng-SRE): Actionable alerts: when a route crosses thresholds, create incident channel and include a prefilled runbook link. Can we auto-attach sample traces?

eldar (Observability): We'll supply a drilldown link to traces with pre-applied filters (route, rollout_id, time). Also include a link to infra metrics (GPU mem usage) for OOMs.

omar (Platform): Quick open questions before I write RFC:
1) exact metric names and tag set (we have a draft above)
2) sampling policy for traces/events
3) dashboard ownership + alert thresholds
4) rollout UX annotations + expected fields on metrics (rollout_id)
5) quotas/cost impact for telemetry ingestion — need estimates

kevin (Eng-Runtime): On quotas: bulk counters are cheap, histograms cost more. Keep 50ms bucket histograms for request.duration and 95/99p in pipeline to reduce cardinality.

eldar (Observability): I'll run rough ingestion estimate once we have per-request emission plan (counters + occasional histograms + sampled traces).

maria (Eng-ML): I'll prep the wrapper PR that adds model_family/version_bucket tags and a test.

omar (Platform): OK next steps (summary):
- I’ll draft RFC and include proposed metric names/tags + dashboard mock (target: next Wed).
- @eldar to provide ingestion/cost estimate (ETA: 3 business days).
- @kevin to prepare runtime patch plan (instrumentation points + low-card tags).
- @maria to PR model wrapper tagging.
- @sophie to provide UX mocks.
- @ryan to draft alert threshold suggestions for SLO team to review.

sophie (Product): :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: telemetry/observability-configs -> staging (build 4872)

kevin (Eng-Runtime): Will run a small canary emitting the new counter names to a sandbox metrics namespace so we can validate dashboards before prod.

omar (Platform): Perfect. If you see anything missing or strong objections, call it out now; otherwise I'll start the RFC and tag folks.

maria (Eng-ML): no objections.

ryan (Eng-SRE): No objections — please include noise reduction guidance (ex: suppress alerts for known noisy routes).

eldar (Observability): I'll add recommended aggregation windows and retention for each metric type in the RFC.

omar (Platform): Thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC link here when ready. :rocket:
